_doc: Decompose the WAL-path cardinality cliff: is it the fsync BARRIERS or the WAL write machinery? Three arms at the same cardinality: (1) wal-normal = syncfs+fsync on (the cliff), (2) wal-nofsync = --unsafe-disable-fsync on (keeps the full WAL write path — staging, register_dirty, group-commit, per-stream data-file writes — but no-ops every device barrier), (3) memory = no WAL at all. If wal-nofsync jumps to ~memory throughput and flattens, the cliff is the fsync barriers. If wal-nofsync stays cliffy like wal-normal, it's the WAL write machinery (register_dirty / staging / per-stream writes), not the barrier. SRV_STATS (--server-stats 2) now splits append time into applock_us / wrwire_us (per-stream data-file write) / durwait_us (fsync wait) — capture it from the server pod during the 50k cells to see exactly where the time goes. Local kind, relative signal.
